# FAQ-011 Engineering FAQ #11

Revision: Rev A

Question One — What is the correct lubricant part number to stock and use on Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03)?
Answer — The lubricant part number for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is CFW-LUB-188.

Background and rationale:
- The induction coil support bearings and the drive coupling on EQ-P1-L1-IH03 were qualified with lubricant CFW-LUB-188 during commissioning. Using the specified part ensures compatibility with the bearing materials and the high frequency environment of the heater.
- Using the exact part CFW-LUB-188 avoids cross-contamination risks from general-purpose lubricants that are not rated for induction equipment.

Examples of correct usage:
- Replace grease during scheduled bearing maintenance with CFW-LUB-188 as described in the equipment lubrication checklist in SOP-P1-L1-01.
- Use OEM-approved dispensing fittings and avoid mixing partial containers from different lots.

Records to keep:
- Log of lubricant lot number, quantity used, and maintenance task in the equipment maintenance record for EQ-P1-L1-IH03.
- Retain a copy of the purchase order referencing CFW-LUB-188 for traceability.

See also: SOP-P1-L1-01 for lubrication procedures and SB-1029 for material compatibility guidance.

Question Two — What lubricant part number must be used for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02)?
Answer — The lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is CFW-LUB-497.

Background and rationale:
- EQ-P1-L3-HP02 requires a hydraulic fluid and slideway compound that meet specific viscosity and anti-wear characteristics. CFW-LUB-497 was selected during equipment validation for those properties and for compatibility with seal materials.
- Use of CFW-LUB-497 supports consistent press performance and reduces the likelihood of seal degradation.

Examples of correct usage:
- Top up hydraulic reservoirs and apply slideway lubricant using CFW-LUB-497 per the press maintenance routine in SOP-P1-L3-04.
- When changing suppliers, verify that the replacement item references CFW-LUB-497 to maintain specification continuity.

Records to keep:
- Hydraulic fluid change or top-up entries in the press maintenance log specifying CFW-LUB-497.
- Batch numbers of CFW-LUB-497 used and the maintenance technician initials for audit.

See also: SOP-P1-L3-04 for press hydraulic procedures and SB-1029 for lubricant storage requirements.

Question Three — Which lubricant part number is specified for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02)?
Answer — The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930.

Background and rationale:
- The high-load contact points and worm geartrain in EQ-P3-L2-RR02 require an extreme pressure lubricant with the additives found in CFW-LUB-930. This selection is required to maintain gear life under rolling loads.
- Using CFW-LUB-930 minimizes wear patterns known to cause dimensional drift in ring rolling applications.

Examples of correct usage:
- Apply CFW-LUB-930 to gearboxes and point lubrication locations during scheduled service intervals called out in the equipment maintenance plan.
- For spot adjustments during production, apply small measured amounts of CFW-LUB-930 to prevent over-application.

Records to keep:
- Gearbox oil change records that list CFW-LUB-930 and associated filtration steps.
- Infrared or vibration monitoring notes after lubricant changes to document return to baseline.

See also: SB-1029 for lubricant selection criteria and SOP-P1-L3-04 for gear maintenance steps.

Question Four — What is the thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02)?
Answer — The thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days.

Background and rationale:
- The process control for EQ-P2-L3-HT02 depends on accurate thermocouple readings to meet part specification. A calibration interval of 50 days balances drift risk with calibration resource availability.
- Calibration frequency was set based on historical drift trends and criticality assessment in the process control plan.

Examples of correct usage:
- Schedule thermocouple calibration events in the calibration management system to recur every 50 days and notify responsible technicians in advance.
- When a furnace run shows temperature anomalies, perform an out-of-cycle verification even if the 50 days interval has not elapsed.

Records to keep:
- Calibration certificates for each thermocouple indicating date of calibration and acceptance criteria, filed under EQ-P2-L3-HT02.
- Calibration adjustment notes and any corrective actions taken as a result of calibration findings.

See also: SB-1029 for calibration traceability and SOP-P1-L3-04 for calibration procedure steps.

Question Five — What is the coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03)?
Answer — The coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 290 hours.

Background and rationale:
- Coil life and insulation integrity on EQ-P1-L1-IH03 are monitored by runtime. An inspection interval of 290 hours was established from life testing and risk assessment to detect early signs of wear before failure.
- Runtime-based inspection is preferred over calendar intervals for equipment with variable duty cycles.

Examples of correct usage:
- Track cumulative runtime on the heater control panel and schedule coil inspections when runtime reaches the 290 hours threshold.
- During inspection, look for coating damage, loose connections, and signs of thermal degradation; document findings and remediate per SOP-P1-L1-01.

Records to keep:
- Coil inspection checklist entries tied to EQ-P1-L1-IH03 runtime, including inspector name and disposition.
- Repair or replacement records referencing the 290 hours inspection trigger.

See also: SOP-P1-L1-01 for inspection checklists and SB-1029 for coil handling precautions.
